scope: Automatic Git handoff, remote SHA verification, digest guards, clean-state checks and branch durability (src/providers/freestyle.ts prepare/withGitAuth/pushBranch, src/git-handoff.ts, src/safety.ts inspectPersistence, src/coordinator.ts complete and destroy guards, src/config.ts gitTree/push-mode validation)

findings.title: Clean-state guard passes when git status fails; uncommitted work reported as durably persisted
findings.evidence: pushBranch runs `test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"`. A git status that exits nonzero (truncated .git/index, or 'detected dubious ownership') writes nothing to stdout, so the substitution yields an empty string, `test -z ""` succeeds and `set -eu` does not abort. The script then pushes only committed content, and coordinator.complete (src/coordinator.ts:703) unconditionally sets persisted:true, dirty:false. src/safety.ts:38-39 handles the same failure class correctly by checking the exit code, so the failure mode is known but unhandled here.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced locally under /tmp/probe31/p4 with real git and a real bare remote: commit, branch, commit a change, `git add wip.txt` (uncommitted), then `head -c 40 /dev/urandom > .git/index`. The exact pushBranch body printed 'CLEAN-CHECK PASSED', `git status` exited 128, `git push` created the remote branch, script exit 0; wip.txt content exists nowhere in the remote.
findings.recommendation: Capture and validate the status result: `st=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all) || exit 1; test -z "$st"`, mirroring src/safety.ts:38-39. Add a test with a nonzero-status git status.

findings.title: base_commit read from a worker-writable file makes the ancestry guard and review_url forgeable
findings.evidence: pushBranch takes `base=$(cat ${workspace}/.swarmforge/git-base)`, written at :140-142 in the same root-owned workspace where the worker runs (the OpenCode systemd unit declares no User=, and prepare/pushBranch exec with linuxUser:'root'). The only validation of base is `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" "$commit"` inside the same worker-controlled shell, so a worker-chosen base makes it trivially true. review_url at :268-270 is built from that base_commit.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced at /tmp/probe31/p3 with real repo and bare remote: after the worker change commit, `printf '%s\n' "$COMMIT" > .swarmforge/git-base` then the exact pushBranch body exits 0 and prints base == commit, so the reported compare range is <commit>...<branch> while the true base differs. A rewritten or unrelated-root history is likewise accepted.
findings.recommendation: Treat base as untrusted: record it durably in SQLite at prepare time and compare, or verify remote-side ancestry with git ls-remote on the base branch instead of trusting a workspace file.

findings.title: Destroy-time persistence check trusts forgeable local remote-tracking refs
findings.evidence: `git rev-list --count --branches HEAD --not --remotes` subtracts everything reachable from any refs/remotes/*, which the worker can create locally with `git update-ref`. The coordinator persisted-check at src/coordinator.ts:930-941 only guards workers with an active dispatch or a result lacking git.persisted, so a worker that never completed reaches inspectPersistence with no independent proof; the destroy path at :945-955 then proceeds. pushBranch itself fabricates refs/remotes/origin/<branch> at :255, confirming these refs are treated as authoritative.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced at /tmp/probe31/sf: cloned repo with an unpushed local commit on the worker branch; after `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/<branch> HEAD`, rev-list prints 0, and the safety.ts Python extracted verbatim from the target (roots substituted) prints {"safe": true, "reason": "no obvious unpersisted work"} while the bare remote contains only refs/heads/main.
findings.recommendation: Verify durability against the real remote with `git ls-remote <target>` or compare against a SwarmForge-recorded pushed SHA persisted in SQLite, instead of local refs/remotes/*.

findings.title: Workspace walk prunes node_modules/.cache and skips the walk when workspace is inside a Git tree, hiding nested repositories
findings.evidence: src/safety.ts:32 prunes directory names ['.swarmforge','node_modules','.cache'], skipping any .git beneath them. Separately, :28-29 runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` on each root and, on success, does repos.add(top) without ever running the os.walk that would discover nested repositories. Either path lets inspectPersistence return safe:true while unpushed commits exist in a nested repo, so the destroy path at src/coordinator.ts:945-955 destroys the VM without recovery_required.
findings.reproduction: Trigger A at /tmp/probe31/nm: a repo under ws/node_modules/vendored with an unpushed commit; the extracted target script prints safe:true. Trigger B at /tmp/probe31/pr2: workspace nested inside a pushed outer repo whose .gitignore covers the workspace; after pushing the outer repo the extracted target script prints safe:true although workspace/repo holds an unpushed commit.
findings.recommendation: Bound walk cost by depth or entry count rather than by directory name, and always walk for nested .git even when rev-parse --show-toplevel succeeded. Add a nested-repository test.
